timecoded_text_to_speech.text: This is a session devoted to making change at audacious scale.
Tonight you're going to meet a group of truly inspiring, determined, resilient humans.
All of this is part of something called the audacious project, an initiative that is housed at Ted to respond to some of the world's biggest challenges.
Audacious, intrepidly daring, adventurous, marked by originality and verb bold.
It's the people who possess any and all of these qualities who step up to spark change.
So I'm thrilled to be here. Shall we begin?
Yes.
Let's begin.
When faced with the reality that human movement is, in fact, inevitable,

countries have two choices. They can build walls and prisons and separate children from their parents, or they can create fair and transparent legal systems that facilitate safe and organized migration and resettlement.
No one should have to die protecting forests.
Right now, there are 80 public benefit programs all across the country intended to provide critical anti-poverty resources.
So imagine what this can mean for entire communities, when almost everybody can be walking around with unaddressed dress and trauma.
Just imagine if the ground beneath your home suddenly started to sink. That's what's happening across the Arctic.
Thawing, permafrost, threatens everyone on the planet because it stores a massive amount of ancient frozen carbon.
The fundamental problem isn't that farmers have no cash. It's that they don't have it when they need it.
We are at a tipping point for US democracy and, frankly, democracy globally.
Our audacious idea is to ignite a family caregiver movement that will revolutionize the way we experience healthcare.
We will train over 70 million family caregivers across India, Bangladesh, Indonesia, and Nepal.
Every single voter, regardless of their zip code, has access to a process that's both fair and trustworthy.
Our audacious vision is to reach 1 million farmers in the next five years.
We can leverage this momentum and expand, secure, and protect up to 50 million hectares of land and forests.
We will partner the redesign systems to unlock $30 billion in benefits for 13 million eligible people in at least 15 states.
And that's the calling of this moment to redesign our systems to see people, all people.
Thank you.

youtube_description:
Session 4 of TED2022 featured this year’s cohort of Audacious Project grantees, hosted by Head of TED Chris Anderson and Audacious Project Executive Director Anna Verghese with writer, producer, director, and independent film producer Ava DuVernay.

Watch all the TED Talks: ted.com/audaciousproject
Learn more about The Audacious Project: www.audaciousproject.org
Get updates on Audacious Projects: http://bit.ly/AudaciousNews
